name: ABri Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic mutation in the ITM2B gene
Demonstration of amyloid deposits with Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence in tissue biopsy
Presence of progressive dementia and cerebral amyloid angiopathy symptoms
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Genetic confirmation of ITM2B mutation plus histological evidence of amyloid deposits
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing and histopathology; clinical features support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy with recurrent intracerebral hemorrhages
searchTerms: repeated brain bleeds from vessel deposits
brain hemorrhages due to amyloid buildup

pathognomonic.symptomName: Amyloid deposition in cerebral vessels confirmed by biopsy
searchTerms: protein deposits in brain vessels confirmed by biopsy
amyloid buildup in brain blood vessels

common.symptomName: Headaches related to cerebral amyloid angiopathy
Mood changes including depression and apathy

occasional.symptomName: Visual disturbances due to cerebral amyloid angiopathy
searchTerms: vision problems from brain vessel disease
seeing disturbances due to brain amyloid
slight difficulty with walking and coordination

laboratory: Congo red staining positive for amyloid in brain biopsy
imaging: MRI showing cerebral microbleeds and white matter changes consistent with cerebral amyloid angiopathy
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of widespread neurofibrillary tangles and amyloid-beta plaques instead of ABri deposits
Typical onset age and progression differ
Mutation in ITM2B gene but different peptide (ADan) involved
Presence of systemic amyloid deposits including renal involvement
Distinct clinical phenotype with hearing loss and cataracts

redFlags: Early onset progressive dementia with family history
Biopsy showing amyloid deposits with ABri peptide confirmation
references: Campion D, et al. Familial British dementia: clinical and genetic studies. Brain. 1999.
Westermark P, et al. Amyloid fibrils in familial British dementia. Amyloid. 2001.
